title: Only five Reef Check sites have both bleaching states in the same calendar month in 1998-2006 and 2007-2017
abstract: We counted support for before-and-after temperature comparisons in Reef Check records from the Global Coral-Bleaching Database, version 2. For 1998-2006 and 2007-2017, only five sites have positive and zero mean bleaching in the same calendar month in both periods. A less strict match has positive observations in both periods at 53 sites. Their mean temperature change is +0.691 C, with a 95 percent site bootstrap interval of +0.373 to +1.027. All surveys in the same cells change by +0.572 C. Site-only matching gives +0.038 C at 113 sites. A longer period split and a 10 percent bleaching rule give smaller or uncertain changes. Separate Atlantic and Pacific subsets do not give a clear common excess over all-survey warming. The added result is a matched-support audit that builds on prior campaign tests. Selected repeat sites, missing early outcomes, coarse exposure, and unknown survey effort prevent a biological threshold claim. Code, reduced surveys, cell contrasts, all estimates, provenance, and a figure are included.

display.caption: Temperature change from 1998-2006 to 2007-2017 among matched sites and calendar months. Intervals use 4000 site bootstrap draws. All-survey estimates use the same cells as positive bleaching estimates. These are survey temperatures, not biological thresholds.

citations.reason: We extend its heat-tolerance audit with exact site and calendar-month support counts, not independent biological data.
Its audit of missing early outcomes informs our limits on the selected early sample.
